text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Oil minister Dan Etete says there are no plans to raise pump prices and that a current fuel shortage in Lagos should abate by the weekend.
- The provisional ruling council is to meet in the capital Abuja on Wednesday on a proposal from political parties to shift state governorship elections to next year.
- Talks between Nigeria and Britain to end the current mutual ban on each other's aircraft deadlocked.
- Shell and Chevron oil companies are locked in a fierce contest to secure a gas supply contract for the $260 million West African Gas Pipeline project.
- Nigeria and the United States oppose the coup in Sierra Leone in which the democratically-elected president was deposed by low-ranking soldiers on Sunday.
- Money market active as lending rates, which fell to rcok bottom in March, surge to 25 percent.
- Lagos state says it is owing local and foreign creditors 9.7 billion naira.
- Government may set aside 14 billion naira to fund the development and exploitation of the nation's abandoned solid minerals.
- Insurers pay Nigerian government 138 million naira for crash of a presidential jet in 1996 in which the first son of military ruler General Sani Abacha and 13 others were killed.
- The finance ministry is to take over supervision of Nigerian Import and Export Bank, says finance minister Anthony Ani.
